# Commands and results

- `./gradlew :ddd-core:test :ddd-integration-event-http:test :ddd-integration-event-rabbitmq:test :ddd-integration-event-rocketmq:test --no-daemon`: passed all focused core and transport tests in 17 seconds.
- `./gradlew check --no-daemon`: passed the complete repository check in 10 minutes 8 seconds; 212 actionable tasks, 85 executed and 127 up-to-date.
- `git diff --check`: passed with no whitespace errors; Git reported only repository line-ending conversion advisories.
- `comet native check runtime-integration-event-provider-completion`: passed. Receipt: `runtime/evidence/check-receipts/0978f7524fca566f3a7a825fdce9cef3f8fbef48ce86feb7471b4f86c5a0c932.json`.

# Skipped checks

- No live RabbitMQ or RocketMQ broker was started. The provider completion contract is verified at the transport API boundary by exercising success callbacks, asynchronous failure callbacks, synchronous send throws, and duplicate terminal callbacks. Broker publisher confirms and production topology remain explicit non-goals for this slice.
- No HTTP multi-process route reset was exercised. The focused HTTP tests execute the registered capability call boundary deterministically and cover success, capability failure, and an empty subscriber set.

# Spec consistency

- `IntegrationEventPublishCompletion` centralizes the provider terminal transition with an atomic first-wins guard and marks completion before invoking callback code.
- Callback exceptions are contained after the terminal result and cannot invoke the opposite callback or reopen the durable attempt.
- HTTP protects destination resolution, subscriber lookup, envelope encoding, executor submission, and capability execution; an empty subscriber set resolves failure explicitly.
- RabbitMQ message post-processing now writes only event identity and timestamp metadata. Success is resolved only after `convertAndSend` returns, while synchronous and worker failures resolve once through the shared guard.
- RocketMQ protects envelope/message construction and synchronous `asyncSend` failure, then resolves success or asynchronous failure from the installed SDK callback. Duplicate SDK callbacks are ignored by the shared guard.
- The canonical Integration Event envelope, Runtime Jackson codec, Aggregate/Entity rejection, stable subscriber identity, and Runtime-owned reliable Event state machine are unchanged.

# Known limitations and risks

- RabbitMQ completion still represents the existing `RabbitTemplate.convertAndSend` hand-off rather than a broker publisher confirm. Real publisher-confirm semantics remain the dedicated transport contract.
- The reliable Event contract remains at-least-once. A process loss after an external side effect but before durable completion may redeliver; consumers remain responsible for idempotent business handling.

# Conclusion

Pass. Every built-in Integration Event provider now has one explicit terminal completion boundary. Success and failure are mutually exclusive, callback exceptions cannot invert the result, HTTP empty-subscriber and RocketMQ synchronous-failure paths resolve durably, and no tested normal or failed provider path leaves the reliable Event record permanently `DELIVERING`.
